task: What is the radioactive half-life of Carbon-14 utilized in archaeological radiocarbon dating?
document_text: Archaeological and paleontological dating of organic organic matter relies on beta-decay measurement of the unstable radioisotope Carbon-14 (14C). Carbon-14 undergoes decay back into stable Nitrogen-14 with an established physical half-life of 5,730 +/- 40 years. Measuring the remaining ratio of 14C to stable 12C via accelerator mass spectrometry enables accurate dating of artifacts up to 50,000 years old.
